description: Composite four-panel figure mixing one mechanical-property plot with three bright-field TEM micrographs of austenite in Fe–28Mn–9Al-1.2C–3Cr annealed at 550 °C for different times. (a) Engineering stress-strain curves: y-axis "Engineering stress (MPa)" 0–1000 with ticks every 200, x-axis "Engineering strain (%)" 0–50 with ticks every 10; the legend lists exactly four entries — "As-cast" (solid black), "550°C1h" (red dashed), "550°C5h" (blue dotted) and "550°C9h" (teal dash-dot). The As-cast curve lies lowest, flattening near the 600 MPa gridline, while all three annealed curves rise steeply to a plateau slightly above the 800 MPa gridline; the 550°C9h dash-dot curve extends furthest, running to the right-hand edge near 50% strain, whereas the 1 h and 5 h curves stop at clearly lower strain. (b), (c) and (d) are BF TEM images of the 1 h, 5 h and 9 h specimens, each annotated "Dislocation" in yellow with yellow arrows; (b) and (c) carry 500 nm scale bars, (d) a 100 nm bar, and (d) also shows a large rounded particle with faint internal parallel striations. The panels jointly argue that longer annealing removes dislocations (b→d) and raises ductility (a) while κ-carbides set the yield level.

observations.observation: (a) plots engineering stress with y-axis label 'Engineering stress (MPa)', scale 0–1000 with ticks every 200, against x-axis label 'Engineering strain (%)', scale 0–50 with ticks every 10.
The legend of (a) contains exactly four entries: 'As-cast' (solid black line), '550°C1h' (red dashed line), '550°C5h' (blue dotted line) and '550°C9h' (teal dash-dot line).

In (a) the 'As-cast' curve lies below all three annealed curves over most of the strain range, flattening near the 600 MPa gridline, whereas the 550 °C curves rise steeply to a plateau just above the 800 MPa gridline.

The '550°C9h' dash-dot curve extends furthest along the strain axis, running to the right-hand edge of the plot near the 50% strain gridline, while the 1 h and 5 h curves terminate at substantially lower strain.
One curve, apparently the solid black 'As-cast' curve, ends with a short near-vertical stress drop just before the 40% strain gridline.
(b) is a bright-field TEM image annotated 'Dislocation' in yellow text, with three yellow arrows pointing to individual dislocation lines and a 500 nm scale bar at bottom left.
(c) is a bright-field TEM image annotated 'Dislocation' with two yellow arrows and a 500 nm scale bar; the dislocation structure appears tangled into cell walls around a large grain.

(d) is a bright-field TEM image annotated 'Dislocation' with a single yellow arrow and a 100 nm scale bar; a large rounded particle bearing faint internal parallel striations occupies the centre of the field.
The apparent dislocation density is highest in (b) (1 h) and visibly lower in (c) (5 h) and (d) (9 h).
The caption identifies (b), (c) and (d) as BF (bright-field) images of the 1 h, 5 h and 9 h specimens of Fe–28Mn–9Al-1.2C–3Cr annealed at 550 °C.
The citing text states that the plasticity of the 3Cr strip increases gradually with increasing annealing time, while the yield strength does not change significantly after 1 h annealing.
The citing text states that by observing the TEM images the dislocation density gradually decreases with increasing annealing time, as shown in Fig. 11(b), (c) and (d).

The citing text attributes the increase of yield strength to precipitation of nano-scale κ-carbides, and states that κ-carbides mainly precipitate in the first hour of annealing treatment while recovery needs longer time.

The citing text recommends prolonging the annealing time to reduce dislocation density for improved plasticity, noting that longer annealing may coarsen κ-carbides so the time should be further optimized.

subfigures.description: Engineering stress-strain curves, stress (MPa) 0–1000 vs strain (%) 0–50, four curves: As-cast (solid black), 550°C1h (red dashed), 550°C5h (blue dotted), 550°C9h (teal dash-dot). The annealed curves sit above As-cast and plateau just above 800 MPa; the 9 h curve reaches the largest strain (~50%).
Bright-field TEM image of the 1 h specimen, 500 nm scale bar, annotated 'Dislocation' in yellow with three yellow arrows pointing to individual dislocation lines in a dense, tangled arrangement.

Bright-field TEM image of the 5 h specimen, 500 nm scale bar, annotated 'Dislocation' in yellow with two yellow arrows; dislocations appear less dense than in (b) and arranged in cell/wall configurations.

Bright-field TEM image of the 9 h specimen, 100 nm scale bar, annotated 'Dislocation' in yellow with one arrow; a large rounded particle (with faint internal parallel striations) occupies the centre of the field.
